clue.text: Former Cowley workers were makers of traditional jigs

definitions.meaning: Morris cars were built at the Cowley works in Oxford, so its staff were men of the Morris company
Morris dancers perform traditional English folk dances, jigs among them

explanation.walkthrough: Cowley, a district of Oxford, was home to the Morris Motors car factory; morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both car workers at the Morris plant and the folk dancers who perform English jigs.

clue.text: A shock — a radio operator raised prince

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole string of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock
a ham is an amateur radio operator

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a jolt, and a radio operator lifting up a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run A JAR A HAM upwards, giving the answer read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian ruling prince bore this title, a direct synonym for a prince.

clue.text: Souvenir of priest in Roman Catholic surroundings

indicators.note: Roman Catholic is described as surroundings, so its letters enclose the priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest of the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A keepsake of a priest set among Catholic surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; 'surroundings' alone signals the container. Eli is the stock biblical priest of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a keepsake or memento kept from the past, which is what a souvenir is.

clue.text: I criticise a crook making capital

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
crook as an adjective means bad or ill, an informal sense

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a swindler who is out to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal noun but is used as the adjective meaning bad; 'capital' is the definition, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Sailor heading away from ship after damage

indicators.note: the ship's remaining letters come after the damage in the answer

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word for ship, departs

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A sailor leaves his ship once it has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'heading away from ship' as the sailor deserting; it is the signal to drop the ship-word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, a straight synonym for sailor.

clue.text: Most Venetian rebuilding shows natural simplicity

indicators.note: rebuilding suggests the letters are assembled again in a new order
most of a word means it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Rebuilding work in Venice reveals an unaffected style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the last N of VENETIAN to leave VENETIA, and 'rebuilding' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent, unaffected simplicity of manner, the quality the phrase describes.

clue.text: Girl got starting pay after unusually long absence

indicators.note: starting means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A girl was finally paid after being away for a strangely long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes the first letter of each of pay, after, unusually, long, absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Paula is a girl's name, so the clue's girl is an example of one.

clue.text: Exponent of military force

definitions.meaning: in mathematics an exponent is the index a number is raised to
a nation's armed might, as in a great naval nation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponent of' reads as a champion of military force, but the clue splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A power is a mathematical index and also strength, especially a state's armed might.

clue.text: Primitive nervous reaction over song causes minor eruption

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first pieces sit above the song

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original, as in Urtext
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A primal nervous response to a song brings on a small outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' is the medical sense: a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria, or hives, is an itchy rash, an eruption on the skin.

clue.text: Showpieces featured members of the armed forces?

parts.note: to air something is to show it
chessmen are pieces, so pieces are men

explanation.surface: Grand displays starred servicemen.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Showpieces' into show and pieces; the question mark admits that airmen are only some of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are personnel of an air force, one branch of the armed services.

clue.text: College dinner includes a food legally approved

indicators.note: the dinner takes in the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: in Oxford and Cambridge colleges, dinner in hall is the formal evening meal, called hall

explanation.surface: A formal college meal features a dish that has been officially sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, 'hall' is both the dining room and the meal served there.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat is prepared according to Islamic law, so it is food that religious law permits.

clue.text: It comes down heavily on having cats and dogs involved

definitions.text: It comes down heavily on having cats and dogs involved

parts.words: It comes down heavily on having cats and dogs involved
parts.note: pouring rain is said to be raining cats and dogs, and what falls hard then is the downpour itself

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone cracking down on pets; it is the idiom 'raining cats and dogs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from clouds is what comes down in a heavy downpour.

clue.text: A notorious landlord can harm moves

indicators.note: moves tells us the letters change places to form a new word

explanation.surface: A notorious landlord is capable of causing damage when he acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Rachman was a London slum landlord of the 1950s whose name became a byword for exploitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachman's name stands for a ruthless, exploiting landlord, so he is the notorious landlord.

clue.text: Form of torture that may involve hammer and anvil

definitions.text: Form of torture that may involve hammer and anvil

parts.words: Form of torture that may involve hammer and anvil
parts.note: the hammer and anvil are small bones of the middle ear, so the pain is in the ear

explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a smithy torture chamber; the hammer (malleus) and anvil (incus) are bones inside the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear pain is a miserable torment centred on the hearing organ that contains those bones.

clue.text: Malt spirits rancher only abandoned with job

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A rancher quits his job and turns to whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges RANCHERONLY together with JOB; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: John Barleycorn is the folk personification of barley and the malt liquors made from it.

clue.text: Aftermath of stampede shook farm badly

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cattle stampede shook the farm severely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of SHOOK FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede leaves hoof prints all over the ground, the marks left once it has passed.

clue.text: President's retreat from temporary settlement with Israel's leader

parts.note: a camp is a temporary place to live
King David led ancient Israel

explanation.surface: A head of state withdraws from a makeshift settlement with an Israeli leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Israel's leader' tempts as I, the first letter of Israel; it is King David.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp David is the US president's country retreat in Maryland.

clue.text: Watery monster put out to dry

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed monster of Greek myth
to ted is to spread out mown hay to dry

explanation.surface: A water serpent was laid out to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is a farming word: to spread hay out so it dries.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrated means combined with or full of water, so watery fits loosely.

clue.text: Shares concern, keeping some competition restrained

parts.note: holding means keeping or retaining

indicators.note: restrained means held back, so the word is cut short

parts.note: any and some are interchangeable, as in have you any

explanation.surface: A firm restricts competition by keeping part of it under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained' cuts competition down to COMP, its everyday short form, as in a newspaper comp; 'Shares concern' is a firm dealing in shares, not worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding company is a business whose concern is owning shares in other firms.

clue.text: A major cause of current downturn in North America

definitions.text: A major cause of current downturn in North America

parts.words: A major cause of current downturn in North America
parts.note: reads as economic decline, but it means great falls turning a river's flow downward

explanation.walkthrough: 'current downturn' suggests a recession; it is a river current plunging over falls on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara Falls send a river's current plunging down, a major waterfall in North America.

clue.text: Tea including different type of bun

indicators.note: the word for tea takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: cha is informal British slang for tea
else means other or different

explanation.surface: Tea time featuring a different kind of bun.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a sticky British currant bun rolled in a spiral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chelsea bun is a well-known British sweet bun, so it is a type of bun.

clue.text: Chap's given time to one who wanders up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rover roams or wanders

explanation.surface: A man is given some time to someone who drifts about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the wanderer into REVOR, which follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a man's name, so the chap is an example of one.

clue.text: Italian region with a good name in their capital

indicators.note: in means the short pieces sit inside the capital

parts.note: Roma is the Italians' own name for Rome

explanation.surface: An Italian region enjoys a good name in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to Italians, so the capital is ROMA in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Romagna is a historic region of northern Italy, now part of Emilia-Romagna.

clue.text: Light-heartedly good year, without trouble

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so good and year enclose the trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A carefree, good year passes with no troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: G and Y wrap round AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaily means cheerfully and without care, matching light-heartedly as adverbs.

clue.text: One showing ultimate possession, as Tannhäuser does?

definitions.text: One showing ultimate possession, as Tannhäuser does

parts.words: One showing ultimate possession, as Tannhäuser does
parts.note: the final consumer who ends up owning a product, and also a name whose ending spells user

explanation.walkthrough: Tannhäuser, Wagner's opera, ends in the letters U-S-E-R, so it shows a user at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The final buyer or consumer who ultimately owns and uses a product is described by this term.

clue.text: Server at table's no lazy girl

indicators.note: no tells us that the following word is taken away from the server

parts.note: a lazy Susan is a revolving serving tray set on a dining table
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waitress insists she is no idle young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A lazy Susan is a rotating serving stand placed in the middle of a dining table; the surface makes 'Server' a waitress.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Musical instruments untouched by son

parts.note: virginal means pure and untouched

explanation.surface: Instruments nobody has played, as far as the son is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: The virginals are a small Tudor keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginals are early keyboard instruments, so they are musical instruments.

clue.text: Come over to look after baby after six

indicators.note: the babysitting piece is placed after the Roman numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to babysit

explanation.surface: Someone drops round to mind the baby after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'after' belongs inside 'look after baby'; only the second one is the placing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit is to come over to someone's home, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Stiff with age, privileged prisoner gets time off

indicators.note: off means the time letter is taken away

parts.note: a trusty is a prisoner given privileges for good behaviour

explanation.surface: A trusted inmate, stiffened by years, earns remission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets time off' looks like early release; it removes T from TRUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes joints or machinery stiffened and corroded with age.

clue.text: Two men on an exclusion order for being profligate

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the men come after the order

parts.note: an gives the letter A, the indefinite article
a ban excludes or prohibits
Don is a man's name
Ed is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men subject to an exclusion order for dissolute behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two men' supplies two separate names; 'profligate' is the sense of abandoned meaning given up to vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wholly given up to vice, which is what profligate means.
